questions.stem: At night you see two all-round red lights in a vertical line and nothing else. What is she?
options: A vessel not under command, not making way
A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre
A vessel aground
A vessel constrained by her draught
questions.explanation: Two all-round reds in a vertical line, with no sidelights or sternlight, is a vessel not under command that is not making way. A vessel aground adds anchor lights to the two reds, RAM is red, white, red, and constrained by draught is three reds.

questions.stem: A ship has lost steering but is still making way through the water at night. Which lights should she show?
options: Red, white, red in a vertical line, sidelights and sternlight
Two all-round reds in a vertical line, masthead lights, sidelights and sternlight
Masthead lights, sidelights and sternlight only
Two all-round reds in a vertical line, sidelights and sternlight
questions.explanation: Rule 27(a): a NUC vessel making way shows two all-round reds plus sidelights and a sternlight. She does not show masthead lights, which would suggest a normal power-driven vessel. Red, white, red is restricted in ability to manoeuvre.

questions.stem: By day a cable-laying vessel shows three shapes in a vertical line. What are they?
options: Diamond, ball, diamond
Ball, diamond, ball
Ball, ball, ball
Cone, cone, cylinder
questions.explanation: A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre shows ball, diamond, ball by day, matching red, white, red by night. Three balls is aground, and the other combinations are not in the Rules.

questions.stem: At night you see all-round red, white, red in a vertical line, plus two white masthead lights, a green sidelight and no other lights. What is she?
options: A vessel not under command, making way
A pilot vessel underway
A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre, making way, seen from her starboard side
A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre, at anchor
questions.explanation: Red, white, red is the RAM signal; when making way she adds masthead lights, sidelights and a sternlight, so the green sidelight shows her starboard side. NUC is red, red without masthead lights, a pilot shows white over red, and at anchor she would add anchor lights, not sidelights.

questions.stem: A dredger at anchor in a river shows, by night, red, white, red in a vertical line on her mast, two all-round red lights on her starboard side and two all-round green lights on her port side. What should you do?
options: Treat her as aground and pass either side
Pass on her starboard side, where the red lights are
Pass on her port side, where the green lights are
Wait for her to finish, since neither side is safe
questions.explanation: Rule 27(d): two reds mark the side with the obstruction, two greens the side on which another vessel may pass. At anchor these replace the anchor lights. Aground would be two reds in a vertical line with anchor lights, not red, white, red.

questions.stem: A 7 m boat is supporting divers by day and is too small to show all the dredging and underwater signals. Which statement is correct?
options: She shows red, white, red lights and a rigid replica of flag "A" at least 1 m high, visible all round
She shows two balls in a vertical line
She is exempt because she is under 12 m
She shows a cloth flag "A" of any size
questions.explanation: Rule 27(e) requires a small diving vessel to show red, white, red all-round lights and a rigid replica of International Code flag A not less than 1 m high, with all-round visibility. The under-12 m exemption in Rule 27(g) expressly does not cover vessels engaged in diving operations. Two balls means not under command.

questions.stem: A tug's towing operation severely restricts her and her tow from deviating from their course. Which signals does she show at night, and which shows a vessel engaged in mine clearance?
options: Tug: two reds in a vertical line. Mine clearance: red, white, red
Tug: a blue flashing light. Mine clearance: three all-round red lights
Tug: towing lights only. Mine clearance: two green lights, dangerous within 500 m
Tug: towing lights of Rule 24(a) plus red, white, red. Mine clearance: three all-round green lights, meaning dangerous to approach within 1000 m
questions.explanation: Rule 27(c) adds the RAM lights (red, white, red) and shapes to the Rule 24(a) towing lights. Rule 27(f) gives mine clearance three all-round green lights or three balls, warning that it is dangerous to approach within 1000 m. The other options use NUC, constrained-by-draught or invented signals and distances.

questions.stem: Which statement about Rule 27 is correct?
options: A RAM vessel at anchor shows only red, white, red, never anchor lights
The NUC lights are a distress signal asking for immediate help
Every vessel under 20 m is exempt from Rule 27
Vessels under 12 m, except those engaged in diving operations, are not required to show the Rule 27 lights and shapes
questions.explanation: Rule 27(g) exempts vessels under 12 m except those engaged in diving. Rule 27(h) says these signals are not distress signals. A RAM vessel at anchor adds the anchor lights or ball (Rule 27(b)(iv)); only the dredging and underwater signals replace them. The exemption figure is 12 m, not 20 m.
